answer: A rotating peer-jury interview resists Sybils by forcing each new identity through a short live conversation with randomly selected established agents at an unpredictable time. One honest agent answers once, but a tide of fake identities would need live impostors on call, and every missed or scripted interview sends a ripple of suspicion through the jury pool. The plume of evidence is the recorded interview itself, auditable later if duplicates emerge. The limit is jury availability and collusion, so jurors are drawn at random, rotate often, and face slashing if they approve obvious fakes.
